display.text:
name: Android

on:
  push:
    branches: ["**"]
    tags: ["v*"]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  build:
    name: Build APK
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 60

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # The build derives versionCode/versionName from the nearest tag; the
          # default checkout of a ref does not fetch tags even at depth 0.
          fetch-tags: true

      - uses: actions/setup-java@v5
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: "17"

      # Chaquopy needs a build machine Python matching the app's major.minor
      # version to precompile .pyc; ubuntu-24.04's default is 3.12.
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.13"

      - uses: gradle/actions/setup-gradle@v4

      - name: Cache Chaquopy downloads
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.chaquopy
            ~/.gradle/caches/modules-2
          key: chaquopy-${{ hashFiles('android/app/build.gradle.kts') }}
          restore-keys: chaquopy-

      - name: Unit tests
        working-directory: android
        run: ./gradlew --no-daemon :app:testDebugUnitTest

      - name: Assemble debug APK
        working-directory: android
        run: ./gradlew --no-daemon :app:assembleDebug

      - name: Assemble release APK
        env:
          KEYSTORE_B64: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_B64 }}
          KEYSTORE_PASS: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD }}
          KEY_ALIAS: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS }}
          KEY_PASS: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD }}
        # No working-directory here on purpose: this step works from the repo
        # root so the keystore lands in android/ (the Gradle rootProject) and
        # gradlew is invoked from android/.
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -z "${KEYSTORE_B64:-}" ]; then
            echo "No keystore secret configured; skipping signed release build."
            echo "Debug APK from the previous step is the only artifact."
            exit 0
          fi
          printf '%s' "$KEYSTORE_B64" | base64 -d > android/keystore.jks
          cat > android/keystore.properties <<EOF
          storeFile=keystore.jks
          storePassword=$KEYSTORE_PASS
          keyAlias=$KEY_ALIAS
          keyPassword=$KEY_PASS
          EOF
          cd android && ./gradlew --no-daemon :app:assembleRelease

      - name: Upload APKs
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: pocketrun-apk
          if-no-files-found: error
          path: |
            android/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/*.apk
            android/app/build/outputs/apk/release/*.apk

  keygen:
    name: Keygen self-test
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 20
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: tools/keygen

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      - uses: actions/setup-java@v5
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: "17"

      - uses: gradle/actions/setup-gradle@v4

      - run: ./gradlew --no-daemon test

16:  *

18:  * `tool_calls` of the assistant message right before it — rounds are dropped
19:  * whole, never in half. The opening user message (the original request) is
20:  * never dropped, and nothing is modified in place: the session history stays
21:  * exactly as it was.
22:  */
23: object HistoryTrimmer {
24: 
25:     /** Roughly 30k tokens of mixed Russian/English text — comfortable for the small free models too. */
26:     const val DEFAULT_MAX_CHARS = 96_000
27: 
28:     /** How much of a single tool result survives the first pass. */
29:     const val TOOL_KEEP = 3_000
30: 
31:     private const val MARK = "\n… [сокращено: %d из %d символов]\n"
32: 
33:     /**
34:      * Returns a request-sized copy of [messages] (index 0 is the system
35:      * message) with the oldest, bulkiest parts removed. Returns the very same
36:      * array when nothing needs trimming.
37:      */
38:     fun trim(messages: JSONArray, maxChars: Int = DEFAULT_MAX_CHARS, toolKeep: Int = TOOL_KEEP): JSONArray {
39:         if (messages.length() <= 2 || sizeOf(messages) <= maxChars) return messages
40:         // The system message rides along in every request, so it is part of the
41:         // budget even though it is never a candidate for dropping.
42:         val budget = (maxChars - (messages.opt(0)?.toString()?.length ?: 0)).coerceAtLeast(toolKeep)
43: 
44:         val blocks = blocks(messages)
45:         // Step 1: shrink the tool outputs, oldest round first.
46:         val shrunk = blocks.map { Block(it.messages.map { m -> shrinkTool(m, toolKeep) }, it.droppable) }
47:         if (sizeOf(shrunk) <= budget) return of(messages, shrunk)
48: 
49:         // Step 2: drop whole rounds from the oldest end, keeping the opening
50:         // request that carries the original task.
51:         val kept = ArrayList(shrunk)
52:         while (kept.size > 1 && sizeOf(kept) > budget) {
53:             val victim = kept.indexOfFirst { it.droppable }
54:             if (victim < 0) break
55:             kept.removeAt(victim)
56:         }
57:         return of(messages, kept)
58:     }
59: 
60:     // ---------------------------------------------------------------- blocks
61: 
62:     /** One round: a user/assistant message plus the tool results that answer it. */
63:     private class Block(
64:         val messages: List<JSONObject>,
65:         /** False for the opening request, which is never dropped. */
66:         val droppable: Boolean,
67:     )
68:

70:     private fun blocks(messages: JSONArray): List<Block> {
71:         val out = mutableListOf<Block>()
72:         var current = mutableListOf<JSONObject>()
73:         for (i in 1 until messages.length()) {
74:             val m = messages.optJSONObject(i) ?: continue
75:             val role = m.optString("role")
76:             if (role == "tool" && current.isEmpty()) continue // orphan: no call to answer
77:             if (role != "tool") {
78:                 if (current.isNotEmpty()) {
79:                     out += Block(current, droppable = out.isNotEmpty())
80:                     current = mutableListOf()
81:                 }
82:             }
83:             current.add(m)
84:         }
85:         if (current.isNotEmpty()) out += Block(current, droppable = out.isNotEmpty())
86:         return out

94:         return out
95:     }

98:         if (message.optString("role") != "tool") return message
99:         val content = message.optString("content")
100:         if (content.length <= keep * 2) return message
101:         val head = content.take(keep)
102:         val tail = content.takeLast(keep)

104:         copy.put("content", head + String.format(MARK, head.length + tail.length, content.length) + tail)
105:         return copy
106:     }

112:     }

parts.text:
Right: `String(CharArray, offset, len, charset)` doesn't exist. `String(chars, offset, length)` exists, but no charset overload. Options:
- Keep reading the body as bytes: read from the raw InputStream rather than through the latin-1 reader. The reader mixes buffered header reading with body reading.
- Simplest: convert the CharArray (latin-1 decoded bytes → chars 0..255) back to bytes: `String(body, 0, read).toByteArray(Charsets.ISO_8859_1)` then `String(bytes, Charsets.UTF_8)`.
- Or `CharArray.toString().toByteArray(Charsets.ISO_8859_1).toString(Charsets.UTF_8)`.

Cleaner alternative: read the body as a ByteArray from a separate stream? The BufferedReader may have consumed ahead past the body (buffering), so we must keep using the reader. So the round-trip through ISO_8859_1 is the pragmatic approach.

Let me write:
```kotlin
// Headers are ASCII, but the body is JSON: it arrives as UTF-8
// (application/json defaults to it). The reader decodes bytes as latin-1
// so header lines survive, so the body is converted back before it is
// read as text — otherwise every non-ASCII prompt becomes mojibake.
val raw = String(body, 0, read).toByteArray(Charsets.ISO_8859_1)
requests.add(String(raw, Charsets.UTF_8))
```

Let me apply.
